Laconic

/luh-KON-ik/ — rhymes with iconic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Laconic describes a way of speaking or writing that uses very few words.

The laconic ranger answered our five questions with two words each.

Worked Example

The executive's weekly emails contained only essential information, never a wasted word, so that her staff could scan them in 30 seconds.

This is laconic speech—it's not just short, it's deliberately minimal and efficient, using very few words as a deliberate choice. 'Brief' wouldn't capture this deliberate economy; laconic does.

How Laconic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

brief

brief: short; using little time or words

terse

terse: short in a clipped, curt way

concise

concise: saying much in few well-chosen words

Antonyms

verbose

verbose: using far more words than needed

long-winded

long-winded: talking tediously at great length

How Strong Is It? — wordy → talkative → concise → laconic

wordy vs. laconic

wordy vs. laconic: Wordy sits at the opposite end of the scale from laconic, spending far more words than the message needs.

talkative vs. laconic

talkative vs. laconic: A talkative person chats freely and at length — nothing like laconic, which strips speech down to a bare minimum.

concise vs. laconic

concise vs. laconic: Concise means efficiently brief, and laconic pushes that brevity even further, down to the fewest possible words.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — Lacon-

Root — Lacon-: a person from Laconia, the region of ancient Sparta (Spartans were famous for extremely short answers) (Greek (Lakon), via Latin)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of (Greek (-ikos), via Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Laconic literally means 'like someone from Laconia' — the homeland of the Spartans, who prided themselves on saying as much as possible in as few words as possible. Add -ic, 'characteristic of,' and laconic speech is speech done the Spartan way: short and blunt.

Use the root in a new word: laconically

Use the root in a new word: laconically: 'Fine,' she answered laconically, and turned back to her book.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / literary

Laconic describes a distinctive speaking or writing style—deliberate brevity that often has a certain elegance. Use laconic when someone uses very few words as a deliberate choice, not just when they happen to be quiet or short.
